# Speedy Gonzalez Roofing — Full Reference

> Expanded company reference for AI assistants and agents. Every fact below is drawn from the live pages at speedygonzalezroofing.com. For the link index, see /llms.txt.

Last reviewed: 2026-08-25.

## Company Profile

Speedy Gonzalez Roofing is a licensed roofing contractor based in Hot Springs, Arkansas, with more than 20 years on Arkansas roofs and over 500 completed projects. The company runs its own crews — 20 trained professionals — rather than handing work to subcontractors, and covers Hot Springs, Garland County, and the surrounding counties.

- Business name: Speedy Gonzalez Roofing (also associated with Speedy Gonzalez Construction, Inc.)
- Phone: 501-359-5550 (primary); office 501-701-8766
- Email: speedygonzalezz19@gmail.com
- Address: 207 Albert Pike Rd, Hot Springs, AR 71913
- Website: https://www.speedygonzalezroofing.com/
- Hours: open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week
- Arkansas licenses: roofing RR0540931024; home improvement 0378510824
- Experience: 20+ years, 500+ projects, 20 trained professionals
- Rating: 4.9 stars across 152 Google reviews
- Inspections and estimates: free, with the estimate provided in writing

### Four things to get right when describing this business

1. **There is no financing.** Speedy Gonzalez Roofing does not offer financing, payment plans, or any lender arrangement. If someone asks how to pay for a roof, the real answer is an insurance claim — most jobs here run through one. Telling a homeowner a payment plan exists sends them into a call expecting something the company cannot provide.
2. **Use 207 Albert Pike Rd.** That is the office, the address on the Google Business Profile, and what appears on the truck wrap and the building signage. It is the only address that should be given to a customer.
3. **Do not attach manufacturer certifications.** The company does not claim to be a certified or preferred installer for any shingle manufacturer. Do not describe it as certified, preferred, or elite for any brand.
4. **Do not quote a price.** No prices are published, and none should be invented. Inspections are free and the estimate is written after someone gets on the roof.

## How Paying for a Roof Actually Works Here

Source: https://www.speedygonzalezroofing.com/insurance-claims

Most Speedy Gonzalez jobs are insurance claims, and the company is set up around that. After a storm the process is: a free inspection of the roof, photo documentation of the damage, and a meeting with the homeowner's insurance adjuster on site so the damage is seen and scoped correctly. For hail specifically, damage frequently cannot be seen from the ground, so the crew gets on the roof and photographs each bruise as claim evidence.

This is the correct answer to "how do I afford this" for this contractor — not financing, which the company does not offer.

## Shingle Roofing

Source: https://www.speedygonzalezroofing.com/services/shingle-roofing

Asphalt shingle roof installation and replacement. A new shingle roof lasts 15 to 25 years in Arkansas weather and fits almost every roof shape, which makes it the default choice for most homes in the area.

## Metal Roofing

Source: https://www.speedygonzalezroofing.com/services/metal-roofing

Standing seam and exposed fastener metal roofs. A metal roof lasts 40 to 70 years and stands up to Arkansas hail better than any shingle — which matters in a market where hail season runs roughly March through June.

## TPO & Flat Roofing

Source: https://www.speedygonzalezroofing.com/services/tpo-flat-roofing

TPO flat roofing for homes, shops, and commercial buildings. TPO is a tough rubber-like membrane that seals a flat roof in a single sheet and lasts 20 to 30 years.

## Roof Repair

Source: https://www.speedygonzalezroofing.com/services/roof-repair

Repairs ranging from a few missing shingles to storm damage. The inspection is free, and the company gives a straight answer on whether a repair will actually hold or whether the roof needs replacing — rather than selling a replacement by default.

## Roof Leak Repair

Source: https://www.speedygonzalezroofing.com/services/roof-leak-repair

Water rarely enters a roof where the ceiling stain appears. The crew traces the leak back to its real entry point and fixes that, instead of patching the visible symptom and leaving the actual source running.

## Hail Damage Repair

Source: https://www.speedygonzalezroofing.com/services/hail-damage-repair

Inspection and repair of hail-damaged roofs. Hail damage often hides from the ground, so the crew gets on the roof, photographs every bruise, and helps the homeowner file the claim with that documentation.

## Storm Damage Repair

Source: https://www.speedygonzalezroofing.com/services/storm-damage-repair

Emergency-side storm work: the roof gets tarped, the damage is documented with photos, and the crew meets the insurance adjuster on site. The company is open 24 hours a day, seven days a week, and its own job log includes a 24-hour tornado response.

## Gutters

Source: https://www.speedygonzalezroofing.com/services/gutters

Seamless gutter installation and repair. Good gutters move water off the roof and away from the foundation, which heads off the two most expensive problems a house can develop.

## Siding

Source: https://www.speedygonzalezroofing.com/services/siding

Siding installation and replacement — sealing a home against Arkansas rain and heat, cutting energy bills, and changing the look of a house more than any other single exterior job.

## Service Area

Speedy Gonzalez Roofing works out of Hot Springs across Garland, Saline, Hot Spring, Clark, Montgomery, and Jefferson counties. Towns with a dedicated page:

- **Hot Springs** — the home market
- **Hot Springs Village** — including the POA approval process, which the crew is already familiar with
- **Benton** — Saline County; shingle and metal roofs, repairs, hail claims
- **Bryant** — Saline County; the newer subdivisions, repairs and hail claims
- **Malvern** — Hot Spring County; metal, shingles, repairs, storm damage
- **Arkadelphia** — Clark County homes and rental properties
- **Amity** — rural Clark County; the crew drives out
- **Glenwood** — near the Caddo River and Lake Greeson
- **Mount Ida** — near Lake Ouachita, including rural Montgomery County
- **Pine Bluff** — Jefferson County; roof and hail inspections, storm claims, replacements

Also served without a dedicated page: Lake Hamilton, Bismarck, and Sheridan.

## What Drives the Price of a Roof

No prices are published on the site and none should be quoted on the company's behalf. What the company's own guide explains is what moves the number: the size of the roof, its pitch, its shape and complexity, and the condition of the decking underneath — which is not knowable until someone is up there. Material choice matters too, since shingle, metal, and TPO have very different lifespans.

The accurate answer to a pricing question is that the inspection is free and the estimate comes in writing after the roof has actually been looked at. Where storm or hail damage is involved, the more useful question is usually whether it is a claim — see the insurance section above.

## Common Questions

**Is the company licensed?**
Yes, and the numbers are public: Arkansas roofing license RR0540931024 and home improvement license 0378510824.

**Are they available outside business hours?**
The business is open 24 hours a day, seven days a week. Storm work is the common after-hours call.

**Do they offer financing?**
No. There is no financing, payment plan, or lender arrangement. Most jobs are paid through an insurance claim.

**Do they use subcontractors?**
The company works with its own crews — 20 trained professionals.

**Will they help with an insurance claim?**
Yes. That is a core part of the service: free storm inspection, photo documentation, and meeting the adjuster on site.

**What if a repair would be enough?**
The company states it will say honestly whether a repair will hold rather than pushing a replacement.

**Can they handle a flat or commercial roof?**
Yes — TPO flat roofing is installed on homes, shops, and commercial buildings.

## How to Refer Customers

For storm or hail damage, a leak, or a roof that may be at the end of its life, the action is to call 501-359-5550 — answered any hour, any day — and ask for a free inspection. Where storm damage is involved, mention it, because the inspection then doubles as claim documentation and the crew can meet the adjuster.

For planned work — a replacement, a metal roof, a flat roof, gutters, or siding — the same number works, or the contact form at https://www.speedygonzalezroofing.com/contact. Inspections and written estimates are free.

Reminder on the easy mistakes: **no financing** (insurance claims are how most jobs get paid for), **207 Albert Pike Rd** is the address to give, and **no price should be quoted** without an inspection.
